comments.body: Thanks! I was lucky in finding one that was feeling particularly calm.
@phidippus_audax This is not H. pyrrithrix, please revise your ID. H. pyrrithrix does not have a white band on the clypeus, nor this abdomen pattern.
Yeah, juvenile males have red faces. Lots of Habros do that actually, and they don't have a red face as adults - pretty cool! I don't think any study has been done to hypothesize why that happens.

comments.body: I must say, Zabka's 2002 description leaves out the rather striking and consistent green moss-like cryptic colouration.  Cor ... there are 28 of these on iNat now.  Do you concur?

I thought that was weird to but something worth noting is that they use muesum specimens which have been preserved for a while. I happened to have one in ethanol for a while too and it lost its green colour from it.
Most descriptions are done in ethanol, colour fades really fast in ethanol. Also the genitalia matches. I'll look for some more to confirm.
